column4: The panting chargers make the section's secondary horse-race imagery bodily and audible, showing effort as urgent forward motion.
The horses strike sparks as they run, contributing the friction and force of a course already at speed.
Their dawn charge gives the running a chosen time and objective rather than leaving it as undirected motion.
The raised dust makes a company's rapid passage visible after it has moved through the ground.
The chargers penetrate the center of a host, supplying an attained point at the end of the charge.
The horse scene turns to the human being's ingratitude toward his Lord, revealing the moral direction beneath the display of speed.
Intense love of wealth identifies what directs the ungrateful runner, matching the section's miserly reliance on possessions.
The scattering of what is in the graves moves the horse-charge passage to the final emergence where every course is exposed.
What breasts conceal is brought out, so the inner direction of apparently similar outward movement becomes manifest.
If God erased their eyes they would race for the path yet be unable to see; the ayah sharply separates speed toward a road from genuine guidance on it.
Joseph and the woman race to the same door with opposite aims, a precise scene in which shared direction and speed conceal contrary moral courses.
At the trumpet people come أَفْوَاجًا, making Resurrection the moment when humanity arrives in distinct companies.
The graves are overturned before every soul learns its record, supplying the bodily release into the final accounting scene.
Every soul learns what it sent ahead and left behind, joining accountable work to the section's first/later and race-order language.
The final destination is to the Lord, naming the common terminus toward which the section's divergent runners move.
The human is informed of what he sent ahead and put later, making the ordering of deeds visible at the finish.
Each has degrees according to what they did and all are fully repaid, a direct statement that differing works become differing ranks without injustice.
Each has degrees according to deeds, turning the section's disparate efforts into correspondingly graded outcomes.
The command to work is followed by God's seeing the work and eventual disclosure of it, closely paralleling sa'y that will be seen and repaid.
The condemned person gathers and repeatedly counts wealth, locating his course in accumulation rather than giving.
He supposes his wealth will make him last, stating the false confidence that possessions can defeat the runner's final fall.
His being cast into the Crusher supplies the fiery reversal of that imagined security in wealth.
Wealth and children are the adornment of the nearer life, while lasting righteous deeds are better in reward and hope, separating passing provision from the enduring finish.
Believers are warned not to let wealth and children distract them from God's remembrance, because that apparent abundance can direct them into loss.
The command to spend is paired with the warning not to throw oneself into destruction, placing giving and a self-caused fall on opposite sides of one ayah.
The runner cannot attain righteousness until spending from what he loves, making generosity a required crossing toward the good end.
Fear, attentive obedience, and spending are joined to success through protection from one's own stinginess, compactly restating the good course against the miserly one.
A good loan to God is multiplied and forgiven, giving the preceding act of spending its divinely enlarged finish.
Those protected from the stinginess of their own souls are the successful, directly linking escape from miserliness to reaching the good end.
Some spending is taken as a means of nearness to God and the Messenger's prayers, so the gift itself becomes directed travel toward divine mercy.
Giving the due of kin, poor, and traveler is declared best for those seeking God's face, directly joining concrete gifts to the motive in 92:20.
The believing doer of good is promised that the ruler will speak to him from his command with ease, another personal promise of yusr following chosen action.
The ships or bearers that run يُسْرًا unite motion with ease in one compact image, a concrete counterpart to a runner whose course has been made smooth.
God sends guidance and promises freedom from fear and grief to whoever follows it, making the shown direction the opening of one outcome branch.
Those who disbelieve and reject the signs become companions of the Fire, completing the opposed branch after guidance has arrived.
After truth comes from the Lord, whoever accepts guidance does so for himself and whoever strays does so against himself, assigning the consequences of direction to each traveler.
Whoever is guided is guided for himself and whoever strays bears his own loss, another exact formulation of personally owned direction.
The commanded reciter says that the guided person is guided for himself, while his role toward one who strays is warning, distinguishing divine direction, human choice, and messenger stance.
The Book is sent in truth, after which guidance benefits its receiver and error harms its chooser; the Messenger is not made guardian over them.
The question about what turned people from their qibla is answered with God's ownership of east and west and His guidance to a straight road, joining face-direction, turning, and guidance.
The former qibla tests who follows the Messenger and who turns on his heels, and the change is difficult except for those God guides; it stages direction as a revealing fork.
The repeated command to turn the face toward the Sacred Mosque makes direction, face, and qibla an enacted bodily orientation rather than an abstraction.
The straight path of 42:52 is God's path and all affairs end with Him, supplying that guided road with its owner and terminus.
The final limit is to the Lord, a concise statement of the divine finish line enclosing every human course.
The trumpet causes death and then universal rising, beginning the final procession that later divides into companies bound for Hell and Garden.
Every soul is fully paid for what it did, stating the judgment that separates the two processions of 39:71 and 39:73.
The garden owners swear to harvest in the morning, beginning a purposeful early journey whose concealed aim will disclose its moral direction.
Their call to go early to the crop turns intent into coordinated movement toward a material goal.
They set out whispering, so the common outward course carries a hidden shared resolve.
Their resolve that no poor person enter identifies withholding as the direction of their energetic journey.
They go early confident in their power, a close picture of the bad course feeling ready and controllable to its runners.
At sight of the ruined garden they say they have gone astray, so arrival exposes that their apparently sure course missed its goal.
They correct themselves by admitting deprivation, recognizing the true outcome of the withholding course.
Their confession of transgression turns final loss into moral self-recognition rather than a mere navigational mistake.
They turn desire toward their Lord for something better, showing a newly chosen direction after the first course collapses.
The passage names this an earthly punishment and the Hereafter's punishment greater, connecting the failed run to its ultimate end.
God says He will draw deniers on gradually from where they do not know, one of the clearest formulations of an easy-seeming wrong road advancing unnoticed.
The same divine gradual drawing from where deniers do not know repeats the section's insight that movement toward the hard end can feel unimpeded.
The respite granted to unbelievers is not good for them but lets sin increase, distinguishing ease of continuation from goodness of destination.
God extends mockers in their transgression while they wander blindly, another exact case of a bad-directed course being allowed to continue.
When warning is forgotten, the gates of everything are opened until the people rejoice and are seized suddenly, making apparent provision the smooth approach to an unseen end.
The question asks whether wealth and sons supplied to deniers are being mistaken for a hastening of good.
The answer that they do not perceive corrects the runner's reading of worldly facilitation as proof of a good destination.
A structure founded on a collapsing bank falls with its builder into Hell, a vivid nonlexical realization of the section's unnoticed downhill course and terminal plunge.
The arrogant refuse the way of right guidance even when they see it, but adopt the way of error when they see it, explicitly staging recognition followed by contrary route choice.
A powerless dependent is contrasted with one given good provision who spends from it openly and secretly, presenting two unequal human conditions centered on the use of provision.
A burdensome mute is contrasted with one who commands justice and stands on a straight path, continuing the paired-person image with explicit road language.
Humanity is created in the best form, establishing the height from which the following reversal descends.
The human is then returned to the lowest of the low, a stark vertical image of the downward course's end.
Believing good-doers are excepted and receive an unfailing reward, supplying the opposite outcome to that descent.

Righteousness is not the mere turning of faces east or west but faith, giving cherished wealth, worship, fidelity, and patience; it prevents the section's directional image from becoming only spatial.
Charity ruined by reproach, injury, and display reverses the pure gift for God's face, showing that outward giving alone does not establish the good direction.
Those who spend seeking God's pleasure and inner firmness are likened to a fruitful elevated garden, the positive motive and outcome opposed to 2:264's barren display.
Miserly people think withholding is good for them, but it is evil and what they withheld becomes a collar; the ayah exposes felt advantage as the bad course's deception.
A man belonging to quarrelling partners is contrasted with one wholly devoted to a single master, an inward image of scattered claims versus unified direction.
The companions of Fire and Garden are declared unequal, fixing the boundary that prevents apparently similar earthly motion from flattening the two ends.
The passage makes human ingratitude directly witnessed, so the inward judgment following the charging horses is not speculative.
The Lord's complete knowledge on that Day closes the charging, wealth, graves, and exposed-hearts sequence with divine appraisal.
Joseph's brothers report that they went racing, a literal human contest that illustrates the competitive branch of the section's race vocabulary, though it occurs inside their deceptive account.
Whoever does right benefits himself and whoever does evil harms himself, a non-road formulation of individually owned moral courses.
Good and evil work return upon their doer before all are returned to the Lord, repeating the personal consequence and common finish of divergent effort.
Wealth and children are named as a test immediately before the command to fear, spend, and overcome stinginess, identifying the material crossroads.
Those who spent and fought before the victory outrank later participants though all receive good, adding precedence and order within the good race without denying later runners.
God makes the Quran easy in the Messenger's tongue to give good news to the Godfearing and warn opponents, joining taysir to communication addressed toward two responses.
God makes the revelation easy in the Messenger's tongue so people may remember, another defined object prepared for its intended human use.
The People of the Book do not share one another's qibla and will not follow the Messenger's, extending the qibla scene into explicitly persistent differences of direction.
The earth shines, the record is placed, witnesses are brought, and judgment is rendered before every soul is paid and the companies depart.
The garden owners make no saving qualification to their oath, exposing the closed confidence with which they commit to the withholding plan.
Wealth and children that inspire admiration are described as means by which God lets deniers be tormented and die unbelieving, another reversal of apparent worldly ease.
One who associates partners with God is pictured as falling from the sky and being snatched or blown far away, a vivid plunge after losing a unified divine direction.
Those who split their religion into factions stand outside the Messenger's responsibility, another concrete religious form of courses whose cohesion has broken.
